title: Music for the masses
paragraphs: Are you one of those people who find the world of Western classical music a bit snobbish and inaccessible? The Proms – or the BBC Promenade Concerts to give the world's largest music festival its full name - might help you change your mind.

For eight weeks every summer, the Royal Albert Hall in London opens its doors to all-comers and puts on a music show that is varied and wide-ranging. Some music lovers want to get as close as possible to the conductor. They are happy to stand up to listen to orchestras and soloists playing symphonies, overtures and concertos by the world's top composers – all for just £5.

The festival has been going since 1895 and has always tried to be informal and relatively cheap. The Prommers – the classical music groupies who like to stand – typify this relaxed ethos. Before performances, they shout out jokes and every time the lid of the piano is lifted they shout “heave” in unison.
One of the highlights of the Proms is the Last Night, which has a worldwide screening. Popular classics are played while the Prommers wave flags and sing along to the catchy tunes.

The Last Night is so popular with audiences that a ballot has to be held - several months in advance - so that everyone who wants a ticket has a chance of getting one. But it has been criticised by some for being too British and jingoistic.

In recent years the Proms have grown so that they now include simultaneous screenings in other British cities, lunchtime concerts, talks, children's Proms, film and rock music, musicals, Indian classical music, and even tunes from the BBC series “Dr Who”. The expanding offer is proving popular with audiences old and new. Perhaps classical music isn't quite so elitist, after all.

vocabulary.term: snobbish [ˈsnɒbɪʃ] adj. 自命不凡的，势利的
vocabulary.entry: snobbish [ˈsnɒbɪʃ] adj. 自命不凡的，势利的
vocabulary.example: My brother is very snobbish about cars.
vocabulary.translation: 我哥哥对汽车的态度十分势利。

vocabulary.term: inaccessible [ˌɪnækˈsesəbl] adj. 难以接近的，不易理解的
vocabulary.entry: inaccessible [ˌɪnækˈsesəbl] adj. 难以接近的，不易理解的
vocabulary.example: Why is opera so inaccessible to so many people?
vocabulary.translation: 为什么歌剧对这么多人来说都难以理解？

vocabulary.term: Proms [prɒmz] n. 逍遥音乐节（BBC Promenade Concerts的缩写）
vocabulary.entry: Proms [prɒmz] n. 逍遥音乐节（BBC Promenade Concerts的缩写）
vocabulary.example: He conducted more than 140 Proms in a period spanning more than 50 years.
vocabulary.translation: 50多年间，他指挥过140多场逍遥音乐节的演出。

vocabulary.term: all-comers [ˈɔːl kʌməz] n. 所有人，前来的人
vocabulary.entry: all-comers [ˈɔːl kʌməz] n. 所有人，前来的人
vocabulary.example: The show is free to all comers.
vocabulary.translation: 这场演出对所有前来观看的人免费开放。

vocabulary.term: varied and wide-ranging [ˈveərid ənd waɪd ˈreɪndʒɪŋ] adj. 风格多样且内容广泛的
vocabulary.entry: varied and wide-ranging [ˈveərid ənd waɪd ˈreɪndʒɪŋ] adj. 风格多样且内容广泛的
vocabulary.example: The book presents a varied and wide-ranging mix of psychological and educational material.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书包含了风格多样、内容广泛的心理学与教育学相关内容。

vocabulary.term: conductor [kənˈdʌktə(r)] n. 指挥家
vocabulary.entry: conductor [kənˈdʌktə(r)] n. 指挥家
vocabulary.example: He was a gourmet, a pilot, a baseball team owner, and an orchestra conductor.
vocabulary.translation: 他既是美食家、飞行员、棒球队老板，也是一名管弦乐团指挥家。

vocabulary.term: orchestra [ˈɔːkɪstrə] n. 管弦乐团
vocabulary.entry: orchestra [ˈɔːkɪstrə] n. 管弦乐团
vocabulary.example: The orchestra is preparing for their upcoming world tour.
vocabulary.translation: 该管弦乐团正在为即将到来的环球巡演做准备。

vocabulary.term: soloist [ˈsəʊləʊɪst] n. 独奏家，独唱者
vocabulary.entry: soloist [ˈsəʊləʊɪst] n. 独奏家，独唱者
vocabulary.example: The young violin soloist received a standing ovation after her performance.
vocabulary.translation: 这位年轻的小提琴独奏家演出结束后赢得了全场起立鼓掌。

vocabulary.term: symphony [ˈsɪmfəni] n. 交响曲
vocabulary.entry: symphony [ˈsɪmfəni] n. 交响曲
vocabulary.example: The orchestra performed Mozart's 40th Symphony with great passion.
vocabulary.translation: 管弦乐团满怀激情地演奏了莫扎特的《第四十交响曲》。

vocabulary.term: overture [ˈəʊvətʃə(r)] n. 序曲
vocabulary.entry: overture [ˈəʊvətʃə(r)] n. 序曲
vocabulary.example: The new digital element of the show begins with the overture.
vocabulary.translation: 这场演出新增的数字化环节以序曲拉开序幕。

vocabulary.term: concerto [kənˈtʃeətəʊ] n. 协奏曲
vocabulary.entry: concerto [kənˈtʃeətəʊ] n. 协奏曲
vocabulary.example: It is better known as a violin concerto, but is thrilling on the piano, too.
vocabulary.translation: 它作为小提琴协奏曲更为人熟知，但用钢琴演奏也同样精彩动人。

vocabulary.term: groupie [ˈɡruːpi] n. 追星族，狂热追随者
vocabulary.entry: groupie [ˈɡruːpi] n. 追星族，狂热追随者
vocabulary.example: The rock star has a group of dedicated groupies who follow him everywhere.
vocabulary.translation: 这位摇滚明星有一群忠实的追星族，走到哪里都跟着他。

vocabulary.term: ethos [ˈiːθɒs] n. 精神特质，理念
vocabulary.entry: ethos [ˈiːθɒs] n. 精神特质，理念
vocabulary.example: The ethos of the company emphasizes innovation and customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司的核心理念强调创新与客户满意度。

vocabulary.term: in unison [ɪn ˈjuːnɪsn] phr. 齐声地，一致地
vocabulary.entry: in unison [ɪn ˈjuːnɪsn] phr. 齐声地，一致地
vocabulary.example: The students recited the poem in unison.
vocabulary.translation: 学生们齐声朗诵了这首诗。

vocabulary.term: highlight [ˈhaɪlaɪt] n. 亮点，精彩部分
vocabulary.entry: highlight [ˈhaɪlaɪt] n. 亮点，精彩部分
vocabulary.example: The highlight of the party was the surprise performance by a famous singer.
vocabulary.translation: 这场派对的亮点是一位知名歌手的惊喜演出。

vocabulary.term: screening [ˈskriːnɪŋ] n. 放映，播放
vocabulary.entry: screening [ˈskriːnɪŋ] n. 放映，播放
vocabulary.example: There will be a special screening of the documentary next Monday.
vocabulary.translation: 下周一将有这部纪录片的特别放映场。

vocabulary.term: catchy tune [ˈkætʃi tjuːn] n. 朗朗上口的曲调
vocabulary.entry: catchy tune [ˈkætʃi tjuːn] n. 朗朗上口的曲调
vocabulary.example: That advertisement uses a catchy tune to attract audiences.
vocabulary.translation: 那则广告用一段朗朗上口的曲调吸引观众。

vocabulary.term: ballot [ˈbælət] n. 抽签，投票
vocabulary.entry: ballot [ˈbælət] n. 抽签，投票
vocabulary.example: Members will vote by ballot to elect a new chairman.
vocabulary.translation: 成员们将通过投票选举新主席。

vocabulary.term: jingoistic [ˌdʒɪŋɡəʊˈɪstɪk] adj. 沙文主义的，极端爱国主义的
vocabulary.entry: jingoistic [ˌdʒɪŋɡəʊˈɪstɪk] adj. 沙文主义的，极端爱国主义的
vocabulary.example: The speech was criticized for its jingoistic remarks about foreign countries.
vocabulary.translation: 这番演讲因包含针对他国的沙文主义言论而遭到批评。

vocabulary.term: elitist [eɪˈlɪtɪst] adj. 精英主义的；n. 精英主义者
vocabulary.entry: elitist [eɪˈlɪtɪst] adj. 精英主义的；n. 精英主义者
vocabulary.example: Many people think this education policy is elitist and unfair.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人认为这项教育政策带有精英主义色彩，且有失公平。

sentences.chinese: 这个音乐节自1895年以来，一直试图保持轻松友好和相对便宜的风格。

sentences.chinese: 逍遥音乐节的亮点之一是在全球范围放映的“最后一夜”。

sentences.chinese: 这种不断扩展的节目正受到新老观众的欢迎。
